title: Design Snake Game
description: Design a Snake game with move, wall/self collision detection, and food-eating growth, using a deque for body order and a hash set for O(1) collision checks.

blocks.text: 1. Problem Statement

Design a SnakeGame class for a device with screen size width x height. The snake starts at (0,0) with length 1. Food appears one at a time, in the given order, at given positions. Implement move(direction), where direction is U, D, L, or R, moving the snake's head one cell. If the new head hits a wall or the snake's own body, return -1 (game over). If the new head lands on the next food cell, the snake grows by one (score increases by 1, tail stays put) and the next food becomes active. Otherwise the snake simply slides forward (tail moves up). Return the current score after each move.

blocks.caption: A deque represents the snake body; growing keeps the tail, sliding drops it.

blocks.text: 2. Pattern Detection

A snake's body, growing at the head and shrinking at the tail, is exactly a deque: push to the front on every move, and pop from the back only when NOT eating. This maps the game mechanics directly onto queue operations, with an accompanying set for O(1) collision detection.

blocks.title: Connection
blocks.text: The deque tracks ORDER (which segment is the tail, about to be removed), while a separate hash set tracks MEMBERSHIP (is this cell currently occupied), a common pairing whenever both fast lookup and ordered removal are both needed.
3. Understand the Problem

Picture the classic snake video game. Each move, the snake's head advances one cell. If it eats the food, the snake gets longer (the tail does not move this turn). Otherwise, the whole snake slides forward by one cell, meaning the tail cell becomes vacant at the same moment the head moves into a new cell.

blocks.caption: The tail vacates its cell in the same instant the head arrives at a new one, unless the snake is growing.

items: The KEY subtlety: the cell the tail is about to vacate does NOT count as a collision, since it is empty by the time the head would occupy the SAME cell in a wraparound scenario, but more importantly, moving into where the tail currently is is legal precisely because the tail is leaving.
Food must be eaten strictly in the given order, one at a time, only when the new head lands EXACTLY on the next active food cell.
Both wall collisions (out of the width/height bounds) and self collisions (landing on any body segment except the vacating tail) end the game.

blocks.text: 4. Understand with Examples
width=3, height=2, food=[[1,2],[0,1]]. Moves: R, D, R, U, L, U.

blocks.title: Answer
blocks.text: The moves produce scores [0, 0, 1, 1, 2, -1] in order, matching the expected output. The final U move goes to row -1, outside the grid, ending the game.
5. How Should We Think?

A straightforward approach represents the body as a list, checking collision by scanning the whole list on every move (excluding the last element unless growing). This works but costs O(body length) per collision check.

Adding a hash set alongside the deque gives O(1) collision checks: before adding the new head, remove the tail from the set FIRST (unless growing, since a growing snake keeps its tail cell occupied), then check if the new head cell is already in the set. This correctly allows moving into the just-vacated tail cell while still catching a genuine self-collision.
6. Brute Force Solution
Track the body as a list, checking collisions by scanning the relevant prefix (excluding the tail unless growing) directly on each move.

blocks.title: Bottleneck
blocks.text: As the snake grows long, each move's collision check becomes proportionally slower, even though most of the body is irrelevant to whether the specific new head cell is occupied.
8. Optimize the Solution

Maintain a deque for the body's order (needed to know which segment is the tail) alongside a hash set for O(1) membership testing. Before checking the new head for collision, remove the tail from the set if the move is not a growth move, since that cell becomes vacant. Then check the set for the new head cell in O(1).

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: A growing-and-shrinking sequence with strict front/back operations is a deque; pairing it with a hash set gives both ordered removal and O(1) membership checks.
The tail must vacate its cell BEFORE the new head is checked for collision, since moving into a just-vacated cell is legal, a subtle ordering detail easy to get backwards.
Growth simply means "skip the tail removal step this turn," unifying the growing and sliding cases into one code path.

blocks.text: 12. Final Summary

Design Snake Game is solved with a deque tracking body order (front is head, back is tail) paired with a hash set for O(1) collision detection. Removing the tail from the set before checking the new head correctly handles moving into a just-vacated cell, while skipping that removal on a food-eating move naturally grows the snake, giving O(1) time per move.
